156 Lucent's General Knowledge
Unification of Germany 1848-71
Like Italy, Germany was also divided intoa number of states Atthe end
of the Napoleonic wars (1792-1815) there were 38 independent _ states;
Germany in which Prussia was the most powerful:
In 1815, the German states along with Austria were organised into
Germanic confederation
In 1848 revolts occurred in every German state and the rulers were
forced to grant E democraticconstitutions To unite Germany and to frame
a constitution for the united Germany, constituent assembly met ie
Frankfurt:
The Frankfurt Assembly proposed the unification of Germany
constitutional monarchy under the king of Prussia who would become
the emperor of Germany: However; the king of Prussia declined the
offer Repression soon followed:
With the failure of the revolution of 1848 to unify Germany one phase
in the struggle for unification came to an end:
Now Germany was to be unified not into democratic country by
the efforts of revolutionaries but by the rulers into militaristic empire
The leader of this policy was Bismarck who belonged to Prussian
aristocratic family: He wanted to achieve the unification of Germany
under the leadership of the Prussian monarchy:
Bismarck described his policy of unification as one of ' blood and iron'
The policy of blood and iron meant policy of war:
He defeated Austria and dissolved the Germanic confederation: Thus
Austria was separated from other German  states_ In place of old
confederation, he united 22 states of Germany into North German
Confederationin 1866_
The unification of Germany was completed as result of Prussia
France War (1870) in which the French emperor Louis Bonaparte
was defeated and captured: This war enabled Bismarck to absorb the
remaining German states into a united Germany:
The formal ceremony at which William I the king of Prussia, took the
title of German Emperor was not held on the German soil. It took place
Versailles in France, in the palace of the French kings:
Europe: After   unification,  Germany  emerged as very strong power   in
First World War : July 28,1914 Nov 11, 1918
Causes The causes of First World War are as under
Militarism This means the dangerous and burdensome mechanism
great standing armies and large navies along with an espionage
system:
